Job Summary
We are seeking a Staff Security Engineer focussing on Data Protection, Privacy and Governance to serve as the senior advocate and practitioner for data privacy, protection, and governance across the enterprise. Working in close partnership with the Data Protection Officer (DPO), Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams, this role drives privacy-by-design principles, ensures compliance with applicable data protection regulations, and builds a strong, engineering-led culture of data stewardship and governance.
This role demands equal parts technical depth, regulatory fluency, and cross-functional influence delivery, team leadership, and stakeholder engagement at all levels of the organisation.
Key Responsibilities
Strategy and Roadmap

Define, own, and continuously evolve the enterprise Data Protection and Privacy strategy - supported by engineers and architects - ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations, industry best practice, and the evolving threat actor landscape including insider risk, advanced exfiltration techniques, and AI-driven attacks.

Develop and own the investment roadmap for Data Protection, Data Security, and Data Privacy - driving successful delivery across the enterprise through transparent backlog prioritisation, risk-informed trade-offs, and alignment to strategic business objectives.

Enable the organisation to navigate data-related cyber risk through innovative, frictionless, and responsive technologies and services - spanning in-house capabilities and external partner solutions - while fostering a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement.

Champion a customer-centric and engineering-led approach to data protection, incorporating machine learning for data identification and pattern maturity, blended security tooling across assets and channels, and behavioural analytics.

Monitor the evolving data protection regulatory landscape - including GDPR, DPDP (India), CCPA, MAS TRM, and other applicable regulations - and translate regulatory change into timely, actionable programme updates.
Engineering and Delivery Partnership

Build and sustain deep partnerships with engineering teams in three dimensions: as design partners - shaping how data protection capabilities are implemented and operated; as customers - understanding their needs as consumers of data protection services; and as delivery partners - driving enterprise-wide adoption of data protection uplifts and controls.

Partner with external technology providers and security specialists to integrate best practice and leverage or build cutting-edge data protection tooling.

Maintain close and productive partnerships with the Data Office and CTO teams to sustain robust, proactive data protection mechanisms.

Embed Privacy-by-Design as a structured engineering practice - defining and governing privacy gates in the SDLC, product design reviews, and architecture assessment processes.
Operations and Service Delivery

Ensure mature, consistent, and high-quality centralised data protection consultancy and operations services are delivered in collaboration with the service delivery team - maintaining clear service standards, SLAs, and continuous improvement mechanisms.

Own end-to-end data protection oversight across the full data lifecycle - from software development and federated control operation through to secure data erasure - driven by a data-centric observability model supported by automation, metrics, and analytics.

Ensure all regulatory and risk management obligations are met or actively managed. Own high-risk audit findings, regulator-identified issues, and self-identified control gaps - driving timely, evidenced remediation and executive-level reporting.

Own the capability budget, balancing run and change investment to maximise risk reduction and strategic delivery.

Own and operate the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) programme across human-centric channels including email, collaboration tooling, cloud storage, and endpoint - ensuring policies are continuously tuned, measured, and enforced.

Own the enterprise data classification framework and data asset inventory - ensuring data is accurately identified, labelled, and governed in alignment with sensitivity, regulatory obligation, and business risk.

Govern Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) processes for all new products, systems, and processing activities - ensuring structured risk assessment and documented decision-making.

Own the operational fulfilment of Data Subject Rights (DSR) - including access, erasure, portability, and rectification - ensuring responses are accurate, complete, and delivered within regulatory timeframes.

Own the data breach and incident response process - including internal escalation, regulatory notification (e.g., 72-hour GDPR obligation), affected party communication, and post-incident remediation.

Maintain and govern the Records of Processing Activities (ROPA) in compliance with GDPR Article 30 and equivalent regulatory obligations across all applicable jurisdictions.

Govern cross-border data transfer mechanisms - including Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs), and adequacy decisions - ensuring lawful international data flows across the organisations global footprint.

Own data retention and secure erasure policy - defining retention schedules, governing enforcement tooling, and ensuring compliant and auditable data destruction across all storage environments.

Govern third-party and vendor data risk - including data protection obligations in supplier contracts, Data Processing Agreements (DPAs), vendor assessments, and supply chain data risk reviews.
Reporting and Governance

Contribute to and champion change across Cybersecurity and Technology as a senior leader, occasionally outside of primary remit.

Define and maintain a data protection metrics and reporting framework - producing regular dashboards, KPIs, and board/executive-level reporting on programme health, risk posture, regulatory compliance, and incident trends.
People Leadership and Culture

Lead, grow, and inspire a globally distributed team of highly skilled data protection and privacy specialists - building a high-performance culture rooted in empowerment, psychological safety, continuous learning, and meaningful impact.

Manage, develop, and retain high-performing individuals across different geographies, often operating in remote and hybrid environments.

Act as a role model for junior members of the Cybersecurity and Technology organisation - demonstrating the behaviours, standards, and mindset expected of a senior leader.

Lead a developer security and data awareness programme - promoting data responsibility, privacy obligations, and data handling best practices across engineering and business teams.
Must Have Requirements
Technical Expertise

10+ years of progressive experience in Data Security, Data Protection, and Governance in a data-intensive, cloud-native environment with a strong passion for security and privacy.

Expert knowledge of data protection and data security including data discovery and classification techniques, information lifecycle management, DLP controls across human-centric channels, privacy-enhancing technologies (masking, tokenisation, differential privacy), and layered control strategies for sensitive data protection.

Deep understanding of advanced threat actor methods used to exfiltrate data, and proven experience designing and operating defensive controls to counter them.

Strong experience applying machine learning and automation to data protection - including ML-driven data identification, behavioural analytics, anomaly detection, and pattern-based classification maturity.

Strong cybersecurity background with demonstrated experience in security automation across data protection tooling, workflows, and compliance processes.

Robust understanding of common industry cybersecurity frameworks, standards, and methodologies including PCI-DSS, FFIEC guidelines, CIS, NIST, ISO 27001, ISO27701, and applicable data protection regulations (GDPR, DPDP, CCPA).

Proven track record of close collaboration with data engineering teams, Data Protection Officers, Legal, and Compliance functions to deliver integrated privacy and protection outcomes.
Stakeholder Management.

Highly credible communicator and influencer - able to engage, challenge, and align senior stakeholders across business, technology, legal, and regulatory audiences with clarity and conviction.

Ability to articulate technical threats, scenarios, controls, and risks to both technical and non-technical stakeholders - translating complex data risk into clear, business-aligned narratives.

Ability to prepare concise presentations, reports, and updates for senior management and board-level audiences.

Strong analytical skills to identify and resolve complex problems, often with risk-risk trade-offs and competing regulatory obligations.

Proven ability to collaborate across industry, academia, and government to solve complex, systemic data protection challenges.

Comfortable operating in fast-moving, complex, and demanding corporate environments - providing clear direction while navigating ambiguity and change.

An ability and willingness to learn, experiment with, and adopt new approaches to achieve business and cybersecurity outcomes across different and often challenging contexts.

A customer-centric approach - understanding how the balance between risk, control, and business need can be transparently and robustly met, including through novel and innovative solutions.

Knowledge and application of Risk and Control Management frameworks, with the ability to manage control gaps and risk exceptions with rigour and transparency.
Nice to Have:

Professional certifications in data protection or privacy - CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT (IAPP), or equivalent.

Cybersecurity certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or CCSP.

Domain experience in Financial Services, Payments, or regulated platform environments.

Experience with cloud-native data security tooling across AWS, - including cloud DLP, data security posture management (DSPM), and cloud-native encryption services.

Familiarity with emerging privacy-enhancing technologies including homomorphic encryption, synthetic data generation, and federated learning.

Experience operating within Data privacy obligations and cross-border transfer frameworks including SCCs and BCRs.

Exposure to AI/ML governance and the data protection implications of large-scale model training and inference on personal data.
Competencies
The ideal candidate is a confident, credible, and inspiring senior leader who combines deep technical expertise in data protection with the strategic and interpersonal skills to drive enterprise-wide change. They are equally comfortable setting multi-year strategy, engaging a regulator, mentoring a junior engineer, or challenging an engineering team on a privacy-by-design decision. They build trust through transparency, operate with high integrity, and are driven by the belief that strong data protection is both a regulatory imperative and a genuine competitive differentiator.
